n-up-pdf.name: N-Up PDF — Multiple Pages Per Sheet
n-up-pdf.tagline: Print 2, 4, 6 or 9 PDF pages on a single sheet — perfect handouts and booklets.
n-up-pdf.metaTitle: N-Up PDF — Print Multiple Pages Per Sheet Online Free | JaurTools
n-up-pdf.metaDescription: Impose 2, 4, 6 or 9 PDF pages onto one sheet online for free. Choose A4, Letter or Legal, portrait or landscape, and download instantly. Private in-browser processing.
n-up-pdf.keywords: n-up pdf, multiple pages per sheet, 2 up pdf, 4 up pdf, pdf imposition online, print 2 pages per sheet
n-up-pdf.quickAnswer: Upload a PDF, pick how many pages go on each sheet (1, 2, 4, 6 or 9), choose the sheet size and orientation, and get a new PDF with your pages neatly arranged in a grid — ready to print as handouts.
keyFacts: N-up imposition places N source pages on one output sheet in reading order.
Each page keeps its aspect ratio — nothing is stretched; pages are centered in their grid cells.
A 12-page PDF at 4-up becomes exactly 3 sheets; empty cells are simply left blank.
Sheet sizes: A4, Letter, Legal — each in portrait or landscape.
A 14 pt gutter separates cells so cut lines are easy to see.
howTo: Pick pages per sheet: 1, 2, 4, 6 or 9 — the live preview shows the grid.
Choose sheet size (A4, Letter, Legal) and orientation.
Click build and download the imposed PDF.
n-up-pdf.formula:
cell_w = (sheet_w − gutter × (cols + 1)) / cols
cell_h = (sheet_h − gutter × (rows + 1)) / rows
scale = min(cell_w / page_w, cell_h / page_h)
sheets_needed = ceil(total_pages / N)

Grids: 2-up = 2×1, 4-up = 2×2, 6-up = 3×2, 9-up = 3×3. Each page is scaled by the smaller of the width/height ratios, so it always fits without distortion.
n-up-pdf.workedExample: A 20-page slide deck at 4-up on A4 landscape: the grid is 2×2, so each sheet holds 4 slides and 20 / 4 = 5 sheets exactly. Each slide is scaled to fit its cell (about 270 × 190 pt on A4 landscape with gutters) — a 5-page handout instead of 20.
benefits: Cut paper use by up to 9x for drafts, handouts, and slide printouts.
Live grid preview shows exactly how pages will be arranged before you build.
Aspect-ratio-safe scaling — no stretched or squashed pages.
Standard sheet sizes with both orientations for any printer.
Everything runs locally; no upload of your documents.
limitations: Pages are placed in order only — custom page arrangements are not supported.
High N-up values make text tiny; 9-up suits slides, not dense documents.
Interactive elements (form fields, links) may not survive imposition.
Rotated source pages keep their rotation metadata, which can surprise layouts.
n-up-pdf.privacyNote: Imposition is computed entirely in your browser with pdf-lib. Your PDF never leaves your device.

faqs.a: It is print jargon for putting N pages on one sheet. 2-up = 2 pages per sheet, 4-up = 4, and so on — commonly used for handouts and booklets.
No. Each page is scaled uniformly to fit its grid cell, so proportions are preserved and the page is centered with even margins.
The last sheet simply has fewer filled cells — a 10-page PDF at 4-up gives 2 full sheets and one sheet with 2 pages.

faqs.q: Can I print booklets with this?
faqs.a: N-up arranges pages in reading order, which is ideal for handouts. True booklet imposition (reordered for folding) is a different layout this tool does not do.
Match your content: landscape slides usually look best on landscape sheets at 4-up or 6-up; portrait documents suit portrait sheets.
Usually not — imposition rebuilds pages as graphics, so links and form fields may be lost. Keep a copy of the original if you need them.
